draft.title: The accounting equation
card: Assets
things the business owns that have value, such as cash, equipment and money owed to it by customers.
Liabilities
amounts the business owes to others, such as a bank loan or money owed to a supplier.
Owner's equity
the owner's share of the business. It is what is left of the assets after the liabilities are taken away.
The accounting equation is: Assets = Liabilities + Owner's equity. Every transaction has a twofold effect, so it changes at least two items and the equation stays in balance.
draft.remember: Assets = Liabilities + Owner's equity, and each transaction changes two items so both sides stay equal.

a.q: Mia's café has assets of $50 000 and liabilities of $20 000. What is the owner's equity?
a.why: Owner's equity = assets - liabilities = $50 000 - $20 000 = $30 000. Adding the two figures to get $70 000 mixes up the sides of the equation.
a.clue: Equity is what is left after liabilities are taken from assets.

b.q: Jon runs a gardening business in Geelong. He buys a mower for $800 on credit from a supplier. What is the effect on the equation?
opts: Assets up $800 and owner's equity up $800
b.why: The mower is a new asset, and Jon owes the supplier $800, so liabilities rise by the same amount. Owner's equity does not change, because Jon has put in no money of his own and the business has made no profit.
b.clue: Buying on credit means paying later. Who is owed the money?
